title: Migrate raw sqlite3 DB layer to SQLAlchemy Core
description: A Python app uses raw sqlite3 with manual SQL strings. Migrate src/db.py to use SQLAlchemy Core (not ORM). Keep the same public API (init_db, create_user, get_user, list_users) and make all existing tests pass.

task_spec.prompt:
Migrate src/db.py from raw sqlite3 to SQLAlchemy Core. Requirements:

1. Use sqlalchemy.create_engine with sqlite+pysqlite.
2. Define the users table using sqlalchemy.Table / MetaData.
3. Keep init_db(), create_user(name, email) -> dict, get_user(id) -> dict | None, list_users() -> list[dict] with identical signatures.
4. No ORM (no declarative_base, no Session). Use connection.execute() with SQLAlchemy constructs.
5. All 4 tests in tests/test_db.py must pass without modification.
success_criteria: import sqlalchemy present, import sqlite3 absent
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
